The core operator, totals_side_selection, uses a simple majority rule over bookmaker price discrimination to determine total side. It leverages the fact that standard -110/-110 lines are interpreted as OVER votes due to the <= condition. This introduces a systematic bias toward OVER when no real juice exists. The strict tie-break primitive modifies this by requiring overPrice ≠ underPrice for a vote to count, effectively filtering out symmetric boards. The coin_flip_avoidance mechanism further ensures that when exactly half the books support each side, no pick is made, preventing publication of arbitrary decisions. These primitives form a layered logic where the first filters input, the second enforces consistency, and the third avoids spurious outcomes. The failure mode occurs when all inputs are symmetric, leading to no picks, which is intentional to prevent noise-driven decisions. The historical replay corpus, constructed with only -110 prices, validates these behaviors, showing that legacy behavior produces 100% OVER picks while strict behavior eliminates such deterministic biases.
